title: Tax on taxable income
verbatim_text: (1) Subject to this Ordinance, income tax shall be imposed for each tax year, at the rates specified in Division I or II of Part I of the First Schedule, on every person who has taxable income for the year.

title: Unexplained income or assets
verbatim_text: (1) Where: (a) any amount is credited in a person's books of account; (b) a person has made any investment or is the owner of any money or valuable article; or (c) a person has incurred any expenditure, and the person offers no explanation about the nature and source of the amount credited, money, investment, value of the article, or expenditure, or the explanation offered is in the opinion of the Commissioner not satisfactory, the amount credited, value of the investment, money, value of the article, or amount of expenditure shall be included in the person's income chargeable to tax under the head 'Income from Other Sources'.
provisos: Provided that where the taxpayer proves that the amount was received through normal banking channels from a person resident in Pakistan who is registered with the tax authorities, such amount shall not be added without reasonable inquiry.

title: Return of income
verbatim_text: (1) Subject to this Ordinance, the following persons are required to furnish a return of income for a tax year, namely: (a) every company; (b) every person whose taxable income for the year exceeds the maximum amount that is not chargeable to tax; (c) any non-profit organization; and (d) any person whose business income exceeds three hundred thousand rupees.

title: Assessments
verbatim_text: (1) Where a taxpayer has furnished a complete return of income, the Commissioner shall be treated as having made an assessment of taxable income and tax due on the day the return was furnished.

title: Best judgment assessment
verbatim_text: (1) Where a person fails to: (a) furnish a return of income as required under section 114 or 118; or (b) produce any accounts, documents or evidence required under section 177, the Commissioner may, based on any available information or material and to the best of the Commissioner's judgment, make an assessment of the taxable income or income of the person and the tax due thereon.

title: Amendment of assessments
verbatim_text: (1) Subject to this section, the Commissioner may amend an assessment order made under section 120 or 121, by making such alterations or additions as the Commissioner considers necessary. (5) An assessment order in respect of which the Commissioner has definite information acquired from an audit or otherwise that the income chargeable to tax has been under-assessed, or total income has been assessed at too low a rate, may be amended within five years from the end of the financial year in which the initial assessment order was made.
provisos: Provided that an assessment order shall not be amended under this section without providing the taxpayer an opportunity of being heard via show-cause notice.

title: Appeal to the Commissioner (Appeals)
verbatim_text: (1) Any person dissatisfied with any order passed by a Commissioner under this Ordinance, including an order under section 121 or 122, may appeal to the Commissioner (Appeals). (2) No appeal shall lie against an order unless the taxpayer has paid the admitted tax liability.

title: Appeal to the Appellate Tribunal
verbatim_text: (1) Where the taxpayer or the Commissioner is aggrieved by an order passed by the Commissioner (Appeals), the taxpayer or Commissioner may appeal to the Appellate Tribunal Inland Revenue within sixty days of the date of service of the order.

title: Reference to High Court
verbatim_text: (1) Within sixty days of the communication of an order of the Appellate Tribunal, the aggrieved person or the Commissioner may prefer an application, in the prescribed form, to the High Court on any question of law arising out of such order.

title: Recovery of tax from persons holding money on behalf of a taxpayer (Attachment of Bank Accounts)
verbatim_text: (1) For the purpose of recovering any tax due from a taxpayer, the Commissioner may, by notice in writing, require any person: (a) from whom any money is due or may become due to the taxpayer; or (b) who holds, or may subsequently hold money for or on account of the taxpayer, to pay to the Commissioner so much of the money as is sufficient to pay the tax due.
